questions.q: A downstream service becomes slow but does not fail. Why is this worse than it being down?
o: Callers wait and hold threads, so the slowness cascades up the chain
Slow services always return wrong data
A slow service cannot be retried or monitored
Slowness only affects the first caller
questions.w: A failing service fails fast. A slow one ties up threads and connections in every caller, which become slow in turn.

questions.q: Three layers each retry a failing call three times. How many calls can one request create?
o: Up to 27 calls, a retry storm
Exactly 3 calls
9 calls, because retries are not multiplied
Only 1 call, because retries are merged
questions.w: Retries multiply across layers. Retry at one layer, cap attempts, add backoff and jitter and a retry budget.

questions.q: Which requests are safe to retry automatically?
o: Idempotent calls that failed with a transient error such as a timeout or 503
Every call that returned a 400 or 404 error
Payment POST requests without an idempotency key
Only calls that succeeded on the first attempt
questions.w: Retrying a non-idempotent call can charge twice, and client errors will simply fail again.

questions.q: What happens in the open state of a circuit breaker?
o: Calls fail immediately or use a fallback for a wait time
All calls pass through while failures are counted
A few trial calls are sent to test recovery
The dependency is restarted by the breaker
questions.w: Open protects the caller and gives the sick service quiet to recover. After the wait the breaker becomes half-open and probes.

questions.q: What problem does a bulkhead solve?
o: One slow dependency using all threads and starving other calls
Duplicate messages delivered by a broker
Expired tokens at the gateway
Stale entries in a service registry
questions.w: Each dependency gets its own limited pool or concurrency cap, so excess calls are rejected quickly and other work continues.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of jitter in a retry policy?
o: Spread retries out so clients do not all retry at the same moment
Make each retry wait exactly the same time
Increase the number of retry attempts
Hide the failure from the circuit breaker
questions.w: Random variation added to the backoff prevents waves of simultaneous retries, a thundering herd, against a recovering service.

questions.q: A service is overloaded by a traffic spike. What is the better response?
o: Reject excess low-priority requests early with 429 or 503
Queue every request with no limit so none are lost
Increase client timeouts so requests can wait longer
Retry every rejected request immediately
questions.w: Unbounded queues hide overload until every request is too old to matter. Shedding keeps accepted requests fast.

questions.q: Why should a liveness probe not check the database?
o: A database outage would restart every healthy instance and make things worse
Databases cannot answer health queries
Liveness probes run only once at startup
It would hide the failure from the readiness probe
questions.w: Liveness is about whether this process is stuck. Dependencies belong in readiness, which only removes the pod from traffic.
